claim_evidence.claim_text: The pinned repository is a long-lived, multi-channel agent runtime; the bounded case follows one Telegram direct-message path through durable ingress, routing/session state, OpenClaw's embedded-agent runtime, and Telegram delivery rather than treating every bundled integration as ordinary behavior.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the pin and traced path; other channels, hosted services, ACP, Codex, and alternate harness plugins are outside the deep boundary

claim_evidence.claim_text: The representative polling path uses isolated ingress by default, a SQLite-backed deduplicating queue, lane-scoped draining, centralized authorization before cache/dedupe mutation, and retry or dead-letter handling before an update reaches the agent dispatcher.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Durable Telegram ingress before the model
claim_evidence.confidence: high for admitted text DMs in polling mode; webhook, group/topic, media, and non-default policy branches differ

claim_evidence.claim_text: Telegram labels its receive-acknowledgement policy after_agent_dispatch, but the implementation acknowledges that stage when the bot middleware chain returns successfully. Near-limit text and media-group handlers can return after placing admitted content only in process-local timer buffers, after which polling deletes the claimed spool record; a process failure before timer-driven dispatch can therefore lose those buffered updates.
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate; the acknowledgement mapping and buffer/spool sequence are directly observed, but no crash reproduction, incidence measurement, or cross-branch behavioral test was performed

claim_evidence.claim_text: Routing and session identity are separate from channel delivery identity: an ordinary default-account direct message resolves through sender-aware routing but, with the default dmScope, normally uses the shared agent:main:main session; named-account fallback and explicit bindings can isolate it.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Routing is not the same as session isolation
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the stated configuration; deployments can select peer-scoped sessions, topics, agents, or bindings

claim_evidence.claim_text: Execution ownership is nested: Telegram sequential lanes and reply fences protect channel-local ordering, a canonical per-session reply operation coordinates overlapping turns, configured queue policy handles follow-ups, and the embedded runtime serializes work through session and global lanes with cancellation and timeouts.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for mechanics; which layer dominates depends on channel, session sharing, and queue configuration

claim_evidence.claim_text: Each ordinary embedded run resolves model/provider and harness policy, loads runtime plugins and skills, materializes bootstrap files and context-engine state, builds the effective system prompt, and exposes the final policy-filtered tool set to both the model and context engine.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Model, instruction, context, and capability construction
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the normal OpenClaw harness; raw model mode, plugin context engines, provider contributions, and alternate harnesses change the assembly

claim_evidence.claim_text: The model chooses actions inside a programmed acceptance envelope: OpenClaw owns queueing, retries, replay-safety decisions, liveness contracts, compaction recovery, timeout behavior, and terminal payload construction; those controls verify progress and protocol shape, not task correctness.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: A model-directed loop inside a programmed envelope
claim_evidence.confidence: high for mechanics; the not-task-correctness conclusion is bounded to the ordinary path and inspected acceptance conditions

claim_evidence.claim_text: Tool authority is assembled from several policy layers and hooks; schemas are projected for the provider, calls may be modified, blocked, or require approval, and sandboxing is optional with `mode: "off"` as the default.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Tool authority is layered and operator-dependent
claim_evidence.confidence: high for construction and defaults; configuration, plugins, approval backends, and individual tools remain in the trust boundary, and this is not a security-effectiveness claim

claim_evidence.claim_text: Tool evidence has distinct representations: append-only canonical transcript content, provider-facing bounded/truncated copies that preserve canonical history, and an explicit last-resort persisted rewrite used during overflow recovery.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: One tool result has three representations
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the embedded runtime; individual tool formatting and external-service responses were not exhaustively inspected

claim_evidence.claim_text: OpenClaw separates several durable structures: a sessions.json registry, append-only JSONL transcript trees, the SQLite channel-ingress queue, workspace files, and process-local attempt state. Session locks, repair, pairing guards, compaction, and optional transcript rotation mediate reconstruction rather than one atomic turn transaction.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: State is federated across durability boundaries
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the pinned structures; filesystem durability and crash behavior vary by configured paths and environment

claim_evidence.claim_text: The documented default memory plugin supplies file-backed retrieval tools and a prompt-time recall contract; pre-compaction memory flush can append selected durable notes, while ordinary session history, active context, and workspace memory remain different stores and projections.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for implementation capability and documented slot default; retrieval quality, write quality, and deployment configuration are unmeasured

claim_evidence.claim_text: Optional memory “dreaming,” disabled by default, can promote short-term snippets into `MEMORY.md` based on score, recall/signal count, query diversity, recency, contamination checks, and deduplication; it is across-run adaptation without a task-outcome optimization signal.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for selection and default; absence of a task-outcome signal is bounded to the inspected promotion path

claim_evidence.claim_text: Cron and heartbeat are alternate lifecycle/ingress paths that reuse agent execution: isolated cron prepares its own run/session/delivery context and invokes the embedded agent, while heartbeat applies enablement, active-hours, busy-lane, pending-delivery, and session checks before calling the ordinary reply path with heartbeat-specific policy.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for targeted paths; scheduler persistence and every delivery branch were not deeply traced

claim_evidence.claim_text: Optional coordination is exposed through session and subagent tools: a child may receive isolated or forked context, run once or persist when a channel can bind a thread, and return through lifecycle/delivery machinery; this does not itself provide an independent task-success verifier.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for available mechanics; ACP and alternate harness execution were excluded, and effectiveness or verifier independence is not established

claim_evidence.claim_text: Plugins and hooks form a cross-cutting injection surface over model selection, prompts, messages, tools, transcript persistence, sessions, subagents, gateway lifecycle, heartbeat, cron, dispatch, and execution environment rather than one self-contained architectural responsibility.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for available hook surfaces; only installed and enabled plugins affect a deployment, and third-party behavior is outside scope

claim_evidence.claim_text: OpenClaw invests heavily in transport, protocol, session, replay, liveness, and delivery integrity, while the ordinary traced path has no independent semantic acceptance gate. A before_agent_finalize plugin and repository QA systems are optional, external layers rather than default proof of task success.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Recovery is stronger than task acceptance
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate-high; presence and absence in the bounded path are verified, while investment is an architectural inference rather than an effort or defect-frequency metric

claim_evidence.claim_text: The repository provides run diagnostics, trajectory events, usage/cache/compaction accounting, regression tests, local scenario packs, and optional multi-model judged QA; none of those artifacts establishes the effectiveness of a particular OpenClaw mechanism at this pin.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for observability and evaluation capability; private production data and unrun benchmark outcomes remain unknowable

claim_evidence.claim_text: Existing research qualifies rather than validates OpenClaw's mechanisms: memory benchmarks test broader lifecycle competencies than retrieval alone; compaction studies report retention, latency, and variability risks under other protocols; controlled multi-agent evidence warns against crediting subagents without matched comparisons; and feedback/evaluation literature separates reliable external signals, trajectories, and outcomes from intrinsic completion.
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate to low transfer confidence depending on mechanism; none directly evaluates OpenClaw v2026.6.6 or isolates its implementation choices

claim_evidence.claim_text: OpenClaw reinforces TF-001 through TF-006 and adds a new R11 question: adaptive memory/context policy and outcome-driven optimization are materially different across-run mechanisms even when both change future calls.
claim_evidence.confidence: low pending additional cases; this is taxonomy friction, not an approved revision or cross-harness pattern

claim_evidence.claim_text: After OpenClaw, Browser Use is the highest-information next case under the existing batch because it directly tests perception-grounded action/observation and R5/R6 questions; an adoption cohort, Hermes lineage study, programmed-control replacement, or Claude Code should remain alternatives until their specific evidence and selection prerequisites are met.
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate as a sampling judgment, not a factual outcome claim; the maintainer may value replication, adoption, or the supplied closed-source evidence differently
